newsitem.title: GERMANY: German paper processing workers warn over sick-pay.
newsitem.headline: German paper processing workers warn over sick-pay.

text.p: Media union IG Medien on Wednesday warned that Germany's 100,000 paper and plastics processing workers would pull out of existing wage contracts unless progress was made in talks on threatened sick-pay cuts.
The third round of wage talks for the sector is to take place on December 20 and workers will be seeking guarantees for 100 percent sick-pay during periods of illness, the union said in a statement.

If employers did not indicate willingness to enter serious discussions on the sick-pay issue, IG Medien said it had a mandate to pull workers out of their current wage contracts as early as March 31, 1997.
Sick pay has become a sticking point for wage talks throughout German industry.

New legislation has made it possible for employers to reduce sick-pay to 80 percent of normal levels but companies have generally been unable to implement the law because of union protests, especially in the powerful engineering sector.
